title: Escrowed Batch Reveal: Eliminating First-Proposal Bias in Agentic Marketplaces Through Visibility Protocol Design

### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to "characterize and quantify first-proposal bias in LLM-mediated marketplaces." This is a specific type of bias (first-proposal bias) in a specific context (LLM-mediated marketplaces). While several prior papers address related biases, none explicitly focus on first-proposal bias in this context. For example, [1], [2], [3], [16], [17], [24], and [25] discuss positional or order biases in ranking systems, search engines, or learning-to-rank models, but these focus on position bias in ranked lists or search results, not the sequential decision-making context of marketplaces. Similarly, [7], [20], and [32] address anchoring or sequential biases, but these are cognitive biases in decision-making or anchoring effects in other contexts, not first-proposal bias in LLM-mediated marketplaces. No prior paper establishes or quantifies this specific relationship.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves defining the "first-arrival selection rate" and measuring how often a customer agent selects the earliest-arriving proposal under standard sequential-visibility protocols (HardGate) in the Magentic Marketplace. This mechanism is specific to the sequential decision-making setup in LLM-mediated marketplaces. While [1], [2], [3], [16], [17], [24], and [25] discuss mechanisms for measuring or mitigating positional bias in ranking systems, these mechanisms are designed for ranked lists or search engines, not sequential-visibility protocols in marketplaces. Similarly, [7], [20], and [32] discuss anchoring or sequential biases, but their mechanisms (e.g., debiasing algorithms, anchoring effect measurements) are not substantively equivalent to defining and measuring a "first-arrival selection rate" in a sequential-visibility marketplace protocol. No prior paper uses this specific mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation involves measuring the first-arrival selection rate in a specific setup: customer agents (gemini-2.5-flash) selecting the earliest-arriving proposal 73.3% of the time under a sequential-visibility protocol. While the specific benchmark (Magentic Marketplace) and model (gemini-2.5-flash) are new, the evaluation design — measuring selection rates or biases in sequential decision-making tasks — is not novel. For example, [16], [20], and [32] measure response order or anchoring biases in sequential decision-making tasks, and [3], [17], [24], and [25] measure positional biases in ranking systems. These prior works use similar evaluation designs (e.g., measuring selection rates or bias percentages) to validate claims about bias. Thus, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is "fairness in LLM agentic marketplaces." Several prior papers address fairness or bias in LLM-based systems or multi-agent interactions, including [6], [14], [19], and [27]. While these papers do not specifically target first-proposal bias in marketplaces, they operate in the same general application area of fairness in LLM-based systems or multi-agent interactions. Therefore, the domain is covered.
